$comment: ★★ A THREAD-LOCAL DEFINITION FOR AN ORDINARY REFERENCE IS REFUSED BY NAME AT THE BINDING (P69 round 4, D-LK-THREAD-STORAGE-DISAGREEMENT-REFUSED-ONLY-BY-THE-WRITER-BACKSTOP). Each arm's archive is ONE DSS static library of two members, built by the lane's Windows debug dsscp (`.orchestrators/p69/work/xa/r4tls/fixtures/build_fixtures.sh`): `member_reader.c` = `extern int shared; int read_shared(void) { return shared; }`, and `member_definer.c` = `int shared = 7;`. main.c defines `shared` with THREAD STORAGE DURATION and calls `read_shared`, so the archive search pulls the reader, whose ordinary reference binds to main's thread-local definition. C23 6.7.2p3 requires `thread_local` on every declaration of one object, and an ordinary reference reaches ONE address for the process where a thread-local is one object per thread. GNU ld 2.42 refuses the same shape ('TLS definition in ... mismatches non-TLS reference in ...') and so does ld.lld 18.1.3 (✔MEASURED 2026-10-07 on gcc 13.3.0 objects, `.orchestrators/p69/work/xa/r4probe/m10` and `m11`). ✔MEASURED before this round's check, the same archives (`r4tls/fixtures/probe_examples_pre.log`): every arm was refused only by its image writer's CRIT-1 backstop, `K_RelocationKindMismatch`, naming SymbolIds and explaining it as an address constant the program never wrote. Now ONE `K_ExternImportAttributeConflict`, before the merge, naming `shared`, both units and `read_shared`. NO `optimizedPipelines` ARM: a refusal builds no artifact for an optimized arm to differ from.
